audit_findings.mechanism: Post-close after-tax interest expense must reduce equity-level OE because debt principal is not separately deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Debt financing increases interest expense and financial leverage and may reduce flexibility under our debt covenants and capital-allocation priorities.
audit_findings.explanation: If the supplied August 21, 2026 completion fact is correct, using pre-close OE and the June 30 balance sheet is a demonstrated perimeter error. The actual closing debt, rate, fees and tax effects remain unresolved, but financing up to $7.0 billion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing filing and capitalization schedule, calculate annual cash interest and tax effects, and rerun every scenario using post-close equity-level OE.

audit_findings.title: The numerator and denominator describe different LNA claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 10.953543 million consideration shares; 15.36% of the 71.289768 million denominator and 18.15% relative to the 60.336225 million legacy-share count; combined-company effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes post-close acquisition shares while OE excludes both LNA operating earnings and LNA financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: When an acquisition is completed, the Company’s consolidated statements of earnings include the operating results of the acquired business starting from the date of acquisition, which is the date control is obtained.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator-denominator mismatch. Removing the consideration shares without changing OE would increase each per-share value by 18.15%, but that legacy-only correction would still leave the bull value near $343 per share versus the $514.77 price. A proper combined-company rerun could move value in either direction because it must add LNA earnings and subtract financing and integration burdens; the $13.5 billion transaction is large enough to be material.
audit_findings.action: Choose one consistent claim and rerun: either legacy OE divided by 60.336225 million legacy shares, or post-close OE—including LNA, financing, purchase accounting and integration effects—divided by the full post-close diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: The QUIKRETE asset-exchange value is missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $3.175 billion acquisition-date consideration, equal to 18.1% of the $17.587 billion base equity value; includes $450 million cash; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The historical continuing-operations OE excludes the disposed businesses but does not provide a full run-rate for the acquired aggregates operations; transaction cash and liabilities must also be reconciled through the latest bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the agreement, Martin Marietta will receive aggregates facilities producing approximately 20 million tons annually in Virginia, Missouri, Kansas and Vancouver, British Columbia, as well as cash proceeds.
audit_findings.explanation: The February 23, 2026 closing is demonstrated by the latest 10-Q. The valuation therefore omits the earning capacity of acquired operating assets valued at $3.175 billion while using continuing-only historical OE. This scale is reasonably capable of changing value. The $450 million receipt should not automatically be added again because the June 30 cash balance may already reflect its subsequent deployment.
audit_findings.action: Build post-close normalized OE for the acquired operations, remove purchase-accounting inventory charges, include maintenance and growth capital needs, and reconcile the $450 million cash and assumed liabilities to the June 30 balance sheet before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: The eight-year trend may mix incompatible discontinued-operation perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: anchor is $16.0 million, or 1.4%, below latest OE; any downward correction from an inconsistent back-cast is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inconsistent 2018-2022 OE changes the log-trend anchor used as the forecast starting point.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has recast all comparative prior-period financial information presented in the financial statements and related notes to the financial statements, unless otherwise noted, to reflect this presentation.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates recasting for presented comparative periods, but the supplied record does not establish that 2018-2022 were independently back-cast to the same continuing-operation perimeter. This is therefore an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error. An upward correction is capped by the $1,129.8 million latest-OE minimum rule, but an overstated historical trend could require an unquantified lower anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every 2018-2025 OE observation from a common continuing-operation perimeter, rerun the log trend, and reapply the minimum of corrected trend and latest OE.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be receiving free growth capital
audit_findings.magnitude: base and bull equity values exceed the zero-growth bear value by $4.225 billion and $7.352 billion, respectively; omitted reinvestment amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental capital expenditures, reserve development and working capital required for growth should reduce forecast distributable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At mid-cycle and during cyclical peaks, organic capital investment generally exceeds depreciation expense as the Company addresses current capacity requirements and positions itself for future growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied model shows 5% and 8% OE growth without an explicit incremental reinvestment charge despite a 9.8% RONTA and filed evidence that capital spending rises above depreciation around mid-cycle and peaks. The precise overstatement is unresolved, but the model attributes 31.6% and 55.0% valuation premiums over the bear case to growth, making the omission reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: For each growth scenario, forecast incremental tangible capital and working-capital requirements using sustainable returns, deduct that investment from OE, and rerun the DCF and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Reclamation obligations may be an unbridged senior economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $353 million ARO, equal to $4.95 per diluted share and 2.0% of base equity value; filed $81 million favorable 2025 revision equals 7.3% of anchor OE; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured reclamation cash payments would reduce OE or require a bridge deduction, while any favorable estimate revision included in OE could inflate the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company incurs reclamation and teardown costs as part of its mining and production processes.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and revision are filed, but the record does not show whether maintenance capital, operating costs and OE adjustments already capture the related cash burden or revision. Accordingly, an uncovered claim or distorted 2025 OE remains an unresolved possibility. The liability alone is modest relative to the base valuation, but the revision is large enough relative to annual OE that materiality cannot be dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Trace ARO accretion, associated depreciation, cash settlements and the $81 million revision through each OE year; then either include forecast reclamation cash outflows in OE or deduct only the demonstrably uncovered liability in the bridge.
